My theory for nearly a decade has been: Quadratum is a video game world. Where FF characters have been in the Disney world, we might have some Disney Cameos in Quadratum, but the majority would be video game characters and worlds. The worlds would likely come from Nomura's games (Yozora being the OG Noctis). Imagine a world where Sora plays Blitzball with an alternate Tidus (OG Tidus). It could also explain the Star Wars world, if they ran with a SW video game (like Fallen Order). They could still have Disney owned properties, but use their video games for worlds. Astrobot proves it's possible too. It could also be justified with the fact that there were few FF characters in KH3, and several references. This could be a give and take, give Disney the spotlight for KH3 and reel it back for KH4. I think the contract could have required a SW world in KH4 too, to still give Disney some spotlight. I also worry that Nomura hoped the give and take mentality would work for Disney, but the concern in development that was brought up during the orchestra show was that Disney wanted to keep a strong presence in KH4. This theory also fits with Jared's theory because if Nomura wanted to hand off KH, he would want to slowly/quickly remove Disney, and KH4 could be that transition. Yozora would be the new hero, traveling between Square properties for brief periods in their lore (a la Disney worlds, during the events, before the events, after the events of the films), before leaving after locking its heart or whatever. Obviously they'd run out of properties quick, but I can also imagine Verum Rex being a 3 games and done thing. Nomura is getting older, and if Verum Rex is successful, then maybe other companies would want their games in the franchise. Just a theory though.

The final Fantasy Retrospective: Planning Stage I need some help with a project of mine. I decided a while ago that I wanted to play every Final Fantasy game, and that has ballooned out into a project to experience the entire series in the context of its contemporaries. I’m playing every main line Final Fantasy game, all their direct sequels, select spinoffs, and a selection of games that either inspired Final Fantasy games or were inspired by them. I need some advice for this project though to help me do it right. Any help with any of these questions would be greatly appreciated. &nbsp; 1\. I think I have pretty good list of JRPG’s (listed at bottom) that are relevant to Final Fantasy history, but I need help improving it. There are a couple of western RPGs on it, namely Ultima and Wizardry, that were big inspirations on the first Final Fantasy game, but I know that there has been more cross-pollination between the genres and I’d love suggestions for that. I’m also pretty sure that action RPGs have had a significant influence on modern Final Fantasy, to the extent that the upcoming Final Fantasy XVI is just straight up an action RPG. But the exact lineage of those games is something I have little info on. My list is clearly light in the last decade or so in that regard, although I’ve got some good picks of games influenced by classic Final Fantasy. Any suggestions are appreciated. &nbsp; 2\. I need historical info on the history of the series. I’ve found a few articles, but any articles, videos, or books that could give me better context on the history of Square and Square-Enix and the people who made these games would be great. &nbsp; 3\. I’m trying to experience these games in as authentic a format as I can, given that I do not speak Japanese. So I am prioritizing original releases with original graphics over remasters or remakes. I am also prioritizing official translations where I can. This brings me to an issue though, which is that Final Fantasy II, III, and V did not receive an official English translation until they were remade years later. I would like to play those games in their original form with an official English translation, or something close to it. Any information on translation patches like that would be appreciated. **NOTE: I am not asking for ROMs or information about ROMs. Only patches.** &nbsp; 4\. One way I want to make this experience authentic to how these games were played when they came out is that I want to rely on period-appropriate supplemental materials for advice and walkthroughs. I would appreciate suggestions regarding strategy guides, magazines, and period websites along those lines. &nbsp; 5\. Two of the main Final Fantasy games are MMO’s. I have already played Final Fantasy XIV up to current content (6.38 at time of writing) so I’m pretty good there. However, I would also like some sort of experience in Final Fantasy XI without having to actually commit to another MMO. How do you even get into FFXI in 2023? What is a reasonable stopping point for it? I don’t want to put another 500 hours into this one game, I’d like some sort of representative experience in it without grinding through 20 years of content. &nbsp; 6\. The most difficult game on this list to play in some reasonable state is probably Final Fantasy XIII and it’s sequels. Originally for the PS3 and Xbox360, it is no longer possible to play these games on a modern Sony console, which is what I own. Because of the weird architecture the PS3 used the PS4 isn’t directly backwards comparable. You used to be able to play an officially emulated version streamed to the PS4 via the PS Now service, but Sony merged PS Now with PS Plus a couple of years ago and dropped the PS3 Final Fantasy’s from the service. You can play the games with backwards compatibility on an Xbox, but I’m not buying a current gen Xbox. I’m already going to buy a PS5, I’m not putting another $500 investment in this project. The games have PC ports, but Square-Enix being Square-Enix they apparently run like crap. The best idea I have for this one is to buy a refurbished PS3 in order to play the games, but I’m open to any better suggestions if someone has any. &nbsp; For reference, this is my tentative games list for this project in rough order of release. Nomura's new interview talks about his vision for FF7R, which is to "correct and unify the distortions in perception" (translation included) I used ChatGPT to translate the first section in this interview, which is about FF7R. The rest is about og FF7's creation and KH4. **Q: This year saw the release of "FINAL FANTASY VII REBIRTH" ("Rebirth"), the long-awaited second installment in the "FINAL FANTASY VII" ("FF7") remake project trilogy. What goals did you hope to achieve with this work?** A: The goal of the remake trilogy, rather than being a "remaster," is driven by the desire to "correct and unify the distortions in perception." Typically, a remake is about keeping the game system and story the same while simply improving the graphics. However, in this case, more than twenty years have passed since the original, and merely enhancing the graphics wouldn't align with the current times. I also believe that players' memories have been significantly influenced by nostalgia. I don't think there are many people who have been continually playing 'FF7' for the past twenty years, so the memories of the past have probably changed slightly in each player's mind. Additionally, 'FF7' has several spin-off works, and there are instances where scenes in these works differ from the original. Therefore, due to the passage of time and the existence of these spin-offs, there are subtle "distortions in perception" in players' memories. If you were to replay it now, you might think, "Wait, was this scene like this? I remembered it differently." This is true for me as well, and especially for Nojima-san, the scenario writer, who was concerned about these "distortions in perception." We aim to bring everything together into a unified whole. **Q: I have certainly felt the "distortion of perception" with the spin-offs. How is this "distortion" expressed in the game?** A: In the latter part of the game, there’s a scene in a white space where Sephiroth is present and Cloud is flying, and various visions can be seen. Among those visions, there is undoubtedly a version of the 'FF7' world that exists in the player's mind. They all represent 'FF7,' but each one is subtly different. It’s as if multiple alternate timelines exist; for example, 'In World A, this person is alive, but in World B, they are not.' These changes are made clear, but each person interprets them differently, memories may shift over time, and there may be discrepancies from the spin-offs. In this game, players experienced several worlds on different layers, and those visions express that concept. **Q: In Rebirth, the world map has made an appearance. Has Mr. Nomura's ideal world map finally become a reality?** A: Yes, this is truly thanks to the hard work on the ground. I believe we’ve been able to present the world map of 'FF7' that everyone, including us, has dreamed of. **Q: Indeed, there are plenty of mini-games and exploration elements. Is this because you want players to thoroughly explore the vast world map?** A: That's right. had this video been released a couple years back, it would've definitely relit my passion towards Kingdom Hearts, fortunately enough, it wasn't needed, for I now truly love Kingdom Hearts, all the way through, start to finish. my story with Kingdom Hearts begins with Recreio, a subscription magazine from way back when, my parents used to buy me every release weekly, I have no idea how many I ended up having, but picture 3 cardboard boxes full to the brim with these 20-ish pages magazines. There I saw it, the manga version of Kingdom Hearts Chain of Memories specifically I believe to be released by Panini, something about that boy holding that key-sword(?) just endeared me, I wanted to find and buy that so much, but never did, eventually I forgot about it; Then one day, while messing with my GBA emulator at my phone, I found Kingdom Hearts Chain of Memories, it was a couple years past that initial connection to Kingdom Hearts, I remember getting so excited to try it, and giving it up shortly after. I tried a couple times but never got too far, if I did go past a world I'd be surprised honestly. From there, a lot of years go past, eventually I learned about these games on the PS2, never got around to find them where I lived to buy, but I was fortunate enough that KH was easy enough to emulate that even my terrible notebook could manage to run all 3 games at 60 fps all the time, someway and somehow, maybe divine intervention. And played I did, kinda sort of, I did get to the final world on both 1 and ReCoM, but never got around to actually beating it. 2 was different tho, I liked it way more, I did everything that I could, I got around to defeating all the bosses, I got around to do literally everything that I could've except gummi ship missions and actually finishing Jiminy's journal. Some other years later, and I got around to play BBS, beat that one, hated to do so, still don't like that game. Also got around to try Days and ReCoded, never beaten both at the time, but really enjoyed ReCoded, years later it would end up being one of my favorites from the franchise. Eventually I learned about DDD, and at the time, in some way or another I ended up playing a bit of every release of Kingdom Hearts, but I was not aware of their significance, the story connecting everything, it was literally just "the Kingdom Hearts for the platform I can emulate", it was just "The Kingdom Hearts for the DS", the one for the PSP, the GBA and the PS2 at the time. With DDD, a little bit older and more curious, I learned that people hated its story, and story was just never something that I took interest at the time for Kingdom Hearts. I wanted to actually buy a 3DS for that game, and Kid Icarus Uprising alone, never ended up getting a 3DS tho, would've only played and beaten DDD years later, like, around 2 years ago on a phone that's strong enough to emulate both. But me being unable to play it made me even more curious, I finally gotten around to learn everything I could about Kingdom Hearts. And so I did, and then I treated that like it was the most convoluted and intricate story of all time, it was a point of pride that I had to force through everyone's throat constantly, looking back I can't help but feel embarrassed. Years later, getting closer to the point of this comment, me about 16-17 years old (now 22), starting his edge phase, I started to dislike Kingdom Hearts, still would go after everything releasing but moreso out of an obligation, be the one who knows everything and also be the one who mocks about it. That's the point that my pride turned into shame, and then again turned into a self aware joke: "yes, I know everything about Kingdom Hearts, and its ridiculous, don't play it, don't consume it, it's trash". Looking back, I can't help but hate this moment of my life. Finally, about 3-4 years ago, KH3 was already out for a couple of years, and I had out of obligation to see everything from it, and so I did. I felt something here and there, even through all my angst I couldn't help myself, but still, a lot of angst. Then I saw that Union Cross was finally reaching its conclusion, having tried to play it in the past and just not enjoying it, although loving to collect the medals. I started picking up the pace, watching just the mandatory cutscenes at that point, following Everglow's videos up to date. And then we get to it, to that scene. Union Cross' trilogy is ultimately about betrayal. The union leaders betray one another, the unions betray one another, your friends don't tell you everything constantly, eventually even your chirity betrays you. But above all else, MoM betrays everyone. His plan born out of betrayal, born out of fear, out of absolute hatred. If you rewatch the movie, you can see how MoM's roles are completely and utterly stupid, given to the worst people possible and sharing bits of knowledge that serve for nothing but conflict, that's was the point, to end in conflict. Learning about that was extremely interesting. But the game was not over yet. We finally got to it, the final battle, and the final betrayal. Your player character, not his very first time speaking, but still impactful nonetheless. Betrays his friends, he betrays the OG darkness, but above all else, he betrays you. Not longer the player's avatar, He's the enemy now, and you have to control his friends to defeat him. But it was all a bluff. Watching that made me feel something, and everything that came before and after that scene. "It takes so much effort to build something, but only a moment to destroy it", not a verbatum of what Skuld said, I imagine, but its a phrase I keep with me to this day. Just all the revelations one after the other, the cutscenes in between with MoM truly explaining his plan for Luxu. Luxu the Traitor; After a long long time, I was hooked again. I loved Kingdom Hearts again. In whatever game I play, I always nickname the main male character Makoto (not because I particularly love Persona 3, I loved the 4 movies but I have no interest in playing the games at all, I still need to change my pfp to Phosphophylite to stop getting confused as a fan of Persona lol, I just really enjoy how the name sounds), the female Lyra, and if there's some pet/monster at his side, it's Orpheus or Harp. But if there's an extra spot, it always goes to Everglow. The name just became meaningful for me after watching that video, watching in a premier, WHICH I HATE TO DO, but not at that time. It's my way of thanking him. Then Damo357 dubs the entire game, and, yeah, I can't help myself but cry every single time that I rewatch those 7 hours of hand picked cutscenes. Damien is the player character's name, he did too much to not deserve it. But everglow is the reason I'm in love with Kingdom Hearts again, why I go back to watch those same moments from KH3 and bawl my eyes out. Thanks for being a third reason of why I love Kingdom Hearts.
